result.strongest_objection: The whole premise that this ADR de-risks the koto→rustia swap rests on the embedding-API layer (priority #5), and that layer is the single piece with ZERO spike coverage and the worst sequencing. The headline 0.93µs bypassed the API entirely (spike lib.rs:833-849 pokes vm.arr/vm.reg directly), so the cost of FromValue/IntoValue marshalling and — critically — rooting/fetching an exported Gc closure across GC cycles (the exact KotoSelector pattern: store handle at koto_path.rs:44, call every tick at line 155) is unmeasured and sits on priority-#1's hot path under gc-arena's branded `'gc` lifetime. Compounding this, 'zero-friction koto migration' is false: grabby's scripts are a different LANGUAGE (Koto) with a different module/export model (`export {…}`/`exports().get()`) that has no Luau equivalent, so every script must be rewritten and the export model redefined. The architecture should not lock until a thin end-to-end API-over-gc-arena slice (subset Luau → real embedding API + serde → reproduce the golden through the API) proves both the ergonomics and the hot-path rooting cost.
missing_considerations: No spike measured the embedding-API marshalling or the DynamicRootSet rooting cost of holding an exported closure across GC cycles on the per-decision hot path (priority #1) — the 0.93µs used direct vm.arr/vm.reg pokes

The ADR does not acknowledge that grabby's .koto scripts are a different LANGUAGE and must be rewritten to Luau, nor that Koto's export/exports() model has no Luau equivalent (Luau modules return one value)
No plan for how the batched decide-N API composes with (or replaces) grabby's scalar per-agent Selector::select trait and its interleaved per-agent ChaCha8 RNG / eps-greedy
string.format is absent from the minimum-viable lib list despite being a major Luau byte-compat surface and common in scripts
Metatables/setmetatable/__index, require/modules, and os/utf8/vector libs are not in v1 scope and the distance to the priority-#4 'full Luau compat' goal is untracked
Parser type-grammar completeness (esp. f<a,b>(c) disambiguation, generics, type packs, type functions) is on the LSP-DX critical path but framed as deferrable
No compile-latency/hot-reload budget guards rustia's heavier fusion+regalloc pipeline against regressing the re-eval edit loop
Which script paths require Luau-byte-identical tostring vs merely cross-arch determinism is unscoped
Locale-dependent character classes in the Lua-5.1 pattern engine (%a/%l/%u) must be pinned to ASCII/C for cross-arch determinism — not noted
result.verdict: lock-with-changes — the execution/value/determinism core is well-evidenced and sound, but three changes are required before locking: (1) demote batched decide-N from 'mandatory scaling lever' to optional P4 (it contradicts the project's own ~4% measurement and doesn't compose with the scalar Selector trait); (2) run an API-over-gc-arena ergonomics+rooting-cost spike and pull a thin end-to-end integration slice forward as a co-equal pre-lock gate alongside P0; (3) correct the 'zero-friction koto migration' claim to reflect that scripts are a different language with a different export model that must be rewritten/redefined. Also restate 'accept-and-ignore types' as 'fully parse, don't typecheck' and rebalance the byte-compat risk weights.

p0.summary: The projected ≤0.5 µs claim HOLDS, and by a wide margin. I added two fused IAUS superinstructions to the walking-skeleton VM (OP_UTIL_F64 / OP_UTIL_Q16) that collapse the entire 4-consideration curve+product loop AND the momentum step into ONE dispatch per action (a per-action utility accumulator). This cut dispatches/argmax-call from 320→35 (f64, ~9.1×) and 219→37 (Q16, ~5.9×) — far past the projected ~3×. The full realistic per-decision time dropped from the 0.93 baseline to ~0.20 µs native (0.2045/0.2027/0.2056 µs/d at n=1000/5000/10000), ~0.237 µs wasm/node, ~0.245 µs wasm/deno. That beats the 0.73 µs reference-Luau bar by ~3.6× native and still beats it in wasm, and crushes koto 4.0/5.9. The Q16.16 fused path reproduces the golden 0x31c6ec2734ea6fa2 bit-identically on native + node + deno.
p0.what_changed: Added 2 opcodes + their handlers to the dispatch loop in spike-sk-rustia/src/lib.rs: OP_UTIL_F64 (24) and OP_UTIL_Q16 (25). Each takes action-idx reg, last-action reg, reads arr[0..4], and computes that action's full utility = product over 4 considerations of curve_kind((a+c)%3, x), times 1.25/MOMENTUM if a==last — the exact math the old unfused inner C-loop did, just without per-op dispatch. Two new program builders (build_argmax_f64_fused / build_argmax_q16_fused) keep the argmax compare/select (NLT/ILT, JMPIFNOT, MOVE, FORNLOOP) as real VM ops and issue ONE UTIL op per action. Net dispatches/argmax-call: 320→35 (f64), 219→37 (Q16). Both fused programs are 13 instrs / 4 consts vs the old 35/27 instrs. Wired into native main.rs (new bench column + fused isolation + fused golden) and wasm (bench_run_realistic_fused, bench_q16_golden_fused) + run.mjs/qcheck.mjs. The maximal-fusion-per-action design is what the prompt's "fused per-action utility accumulator" option sanctioned.

p0.verdict: HOLDS — decisively. Native full-realistic decision ≈0.204 µs (target ≤0.5 µs; baseline 0.93). It beats the 0.73 µs reference-Luau bar by ~3.6× native, and even the wasm figures (~0.237 node / ~0.245 deno) sit under 0.5 µs and under the 0.73 Luau bar — so the claim holds on native AND wasm. vs koto: ~20-29× faster than koto-float(4.0)/koto-int(5.9). Dispatch reduction (9.1× f64 / 5.9× Q16) far exceeds the projected ~3×. The Q16.16 golden 0x31c6ec2734ea6fa2 still reproduces bit-identically on native + node + deno through the fused op, so the fusion is determinism-safe.
caveats: The fused op is MAXIMAL fusion: it collapses the whole 4-consideration curve+product loop AND momentum into one native op (a per-action utility accumulator). This is what the prompt explicitly allowed, and it's why dispatch reduction is ~9x not ~3x. A more conservative per-consideration MAC op (keeping the c-loop) would land between the base and this; I measured the strong form the prompt sanctioned.

Honesty controls held: inputs are the same ChaCha8+fnv1a data-dependent world values marshaled into vm.arr each call; isolation loop rotates inputs per iteration; outputs are black_box'd / XORed into a checksum; the Q16 golden reproducing bit-identically proves the fused arithmetic actually runs (not const-folded or DCE'd).

The 0.204 µs native figure is the FULL realistic decision (VM argmax + the surrounding Rust kernel: eps-greedy/SARSA/drift/mood/contagion). The VM argmax's own contribution is only ~0.06-0.078 µs (floor 0.14, isolation 0.078); the rest is the fixed Rust kernel that any selector pays.

The f64 realistic path has no golden (it's a perf proxy, as in the ADR); I kept its math identical to the unfused program and verified the fused realistic run yields the same world checksum as the unfused VM run. Bit-exact determinism is proven on the Q16.16 path, which does have the golden.

Single machine (Apple M4 Max). The 0.73 Luau / 0.93 baseline / koto numbers are from the ADR's prior measurement on the same machine class; I re-measured the 0.93 baseline here (0.907-0.911) and it reproduced, so the comparison is consistent.
wasm built with plain cargo (no wasm-opt); the wasm-tax-vs-native-floor (~6x) is unchanged by fusion since both base and fused pay it equally — fusion's ~4x wasm speedup is on top of that.
